doc.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024

chapter: Studio work and playing by ear
title: Playing by ear rather than by theory, and advice to students
summary: He hears rather than sees music, calls it a gift from God, and tells students to learn scales, chords and the instrument.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I’m going to see if I can focus on that statement which you’ve said a couple of times, in that you didn’t know what you were doing. Can you tell me, is it sort of like I’m playing this note and I really like it so I’m going to hang on it, but what I don’t know is its relationship to the chord? Can you just talk about that a little bit?

Well you know 80 percent of what I do is from my ear. So 80 percent of what say Sonny Rollins does is from his eyes. He can see things and play — well Pee Wee Ellis. Pee Wee Ellis is a great example. He sees what he can hear. I hear what I can make music from. I could hear things that he can see from looking at it you know. But it was a natural thing with me. But if you write it out, I’m lost. Because I don’t know where — I say well let me hear it. And then they play it and I say, “Okay I’m going to do that.” You know? And I don’t understand chord progressions. I don’t understand how you go from one chord to another. I don’t understand how that works but I can hear it. And it’s a natural thing. I think it’s a gift from God that I can hear things like that. You know? And that is the
difference between what I do and what most musicians do. Most musicians can see and hear, but I can only hear. I can only hear what’s happening. You know?
Yeah. Especially in this period we’re in now where most musicians do the jazz school, jazz education route, that they’re taught about all the chord changes and the scales and all that. So yeah.

But I tell students to first, first learn — because I know most people won’t have it naturally like I do. I know that. And I don’t know why I have it naturally like that, but I tell them learn your scales, learn your chords, and learn your instrument up and down and sideways. Learn all of that and if you can develop your psyche to be a good musician. But if I tell them how I do it, you probably won’t ever learn how to do it. I didn’t learn how to do it like that. I didn’t learn how to do it. I do it because it’s a natural thing with me you know. And I don’t understand why but I thank God that I have it because that’s why I’m the musician that I am you know.
